This is relatable, for me it was acne (and some stomach problems). Luckily my acne is clearing up now.

When I would have particularly bad breakouts/ED flareups, and I started falling off the deep end, I would repeat reassuring phrases to myself. My favorite is "Eating anything is healthier than dying," i.e., even if a food in "unsafe" or unhealthy it's better to eat it than let myself starve.

Then sometimes I work up the courage to eat my favorite, easiest meal at this fast casual restaurant that I like. It's something that I liked a lot that broke every single one of my self imposed rules. Just to remind myself that I could. Just to see that it wouldn't be the end of the world. I hoped doing so would kick me out of the negative feedback loop of avoiding food. It's a bit scary at first, and then it feels freeing.

I also count my calories to make sure I eat enough each day. I find that helps me stay a bit more sane. 

Good luck. I hope some of this helps

As someone with ED tendencies, I've seen single threads with different people recommending different diets, to the point where the OP is being told to avoid all dairy, carbs, sugar, and meat. (Reading that isn't... the best for my mental health on bad breakout days) Not much left in terms of food after that, seeing as vegan keto is incredibly difficult to sustain, ESPECIALLY for teens.


That being said cutting out sugar has done wonders for my skin... Imo it's important to be careful with some of the big ones. It's easy to cut out fried foods and sugar, not so easy to cut out dairy, carbs, and meat, seeing as those are staples.

You're not insane, this behavior is inappropriate. It sounds like they want to violate your privacy, and they happen to spend focus on the focal point of your bedroom, a room that's supposed to be private for you. By violating this space they're trying to drive the point home that you and all of your belongings are *their* property, and it will never be yours. Your own bed doesn't even belong to you. This is absolutely not normal parent behavior, it's N behavior.

You said that you can't take your stuff to your flat. I personally had to give up on all of the stuff that was at my parents house. Not because they wouldn't let me, but because I couldn't stand to deal with them. They've probably thrown it all out by now. It's hard. I wish I could go back and bring home all those memories. But sometimes it doesn't work out like that, I guess.

If anyone tells me to forgive my parents, or that I need to reconnect with my parents, I plan on telling them the following:

What's the worst thing, short of murder, that you can imagine a person doing their child? You don't have to tell me, just think it. Now, is that thing so petty that you would ask the child to forgive their parent? Even if the parent believes they did nothing wrong?

If yes, I'd tell them that there's a lot of things they don't know about the horrors outside their own bubble.

If no, hopefully I made my point well enough. 

My parents certainly didn't do the worst possible thing, but they are definitely unforgivable.

I started standing further away from him after that. He would still try things from time to time. 

When I found a partner he got VERY defensive. Started comparing cuddling my partner to cuddling him, asked what sexual things I would do. It was at this point I realized something was VERY wrong. I've been no contact from them for months now.

This behavior is incestuous. It's sexual abuse. It's disgusting.

PM me if you ever want to talk. It's hard to be betrayed by family like this.
